subject: SIG/CAIQ retention mapping & customer-specific log retention exception
messages:
From: Oliver Sullivan <sullivan@atlasdata.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@atlasdata.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ: retention mapping & customer-specific exclusions

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — Atlas Data is moving quickly on the evaluation. Our security team has a couple of narrow follow-ups tied to the SIG/CAIQ and CAIQ questionnaires, and we wanted to confirm how Redwood maps the controls and what evidence you can provide around customer-specific retention exceptions.

Two asks up front:
1) Can you map Redwood controls / artifacts to the SIG control IDs that reference logging/retention (we highlighted sections in the attached workbook). We need a one-to-one mapping we can attach to our internal assessment.
2) For customer-requested retention variances: one of our use-cases requires retaining ephemeral inference logs for 180 days for forensic review. Your default documentation indicates 30 days for Hosted tenants — please clarify whether a 180-day variance is supported, and if so what approvals and evidentiary artifacts are required (audit trail, deletion certification, export manifest, etc.).

I've attached our questionnaire excerpt (atlas-retention-questions-20280515.xlsx). Can you respond with a mapping and a list of artifacts you can reasonably provide? Ideally we need an initial response by EOD Wednesday so we can move through our procurement and security review.

Appreciate it —
Oliver Sullivan
Head of Security, Atlas Data

Attachments: atlas-retention-questions-20280515.xlsx


From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Sullivan <sullivan@atlasdata.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ: retention mapping & customer-specific exclusions

Hi Oliver — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Looping in Neha (InfoSec lead) and Priyom (solutions engineer) to help with the mapping and evidence pack.

Short answers up front:
- We can produce a mapping between Redwood artifacts and SIG control IDs; attaching a first-pass workbook (retention-mapping-draft-v1.xlsx).
- Hosted customers can request retention increases, but 180 days is non-standard and will require a formal exception process (security review + legal amendment). Dedicated/Private deployments offer more configurability.

Neha / Priyom — two clarifying points before we finalize the mapping and artifacts:
1) The Atlas request mentions "ephemeral inference logs" at 180 days. Are you asking for all inference-level tokens/strings, or a subset (e.g., metadata + hashed request IDs)? Attachment refers to full request payloads — we should confirm exact scope.
2) Do you require a certified deletion artifact (proof-of-delete) for the 30->180 change when/if the tenant later requests purge? That will affect the set of deliverables (we can provide export manifests + storage lifecycle records but a signed certification may need legal approval).

Planned next steps:
- Neha to provide the SIG/CAIQ artifact list and any redlines on the evidence we can supply under Hosted.
- Priyom to confirm technical feasibility and any operational controls we would need to set (KMS config, export hooks, per-tenant TTL config).

We'll aim to get an initial response and the updated mapping to you by EOD Wednesday (17 May).

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention-mapping-draft-v1.xlsx


From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Oliver Sullivan <sullivan@atlasdata.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@atlasdata.com>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ: retention mapping & customer-specific exclusions

Hi all — quick, pragmatic response and list of artifacts we can provide. I tried to keep this scoped to what’s producible within our Hosted offering without immediate engineering changes.

1) Scope clarification from Markus is important: Atlas needs to confirm whether "ephemeral inference logs" means raw request/response text (PLAINTEXT), or the following reduced set: request metadata, hashed request ID, timestamps, and error/latency traces. Retaining PII or plaintext user content for 180 days has additional risk and policy implications under SOC 2 and our data minimization practices.

2) What we can provide today (Hosted):
- SIG/CAIQ mapping: a control-to-artifact spreadsheet mapping logging and retention controls to specific artifacts (audit logs, retention policy excerpt, S3 export manifests, KMS rotation records). See retention-mapping-draft-v1.xlsx attached.
- Evidence artifacts available in an evidence bundle:
  - Audit log extract (timestamped) showing retention policy changes and per-tenant retention configuration history.
  - Storage export manifest (S3 paths + checksums) for any exported payloads.
  - Key management snapshot showing KMS key IDs and rotation metadata (redacted where necessary).
  - Sample deletion manifest (example proof-of-delete) showing tombstone events and object lifecycle transitions.
  - SOC 2 control narrative excerpt describing our evidence retention and deletion process (we will extract the relevant sections).

3) On 180-day retention specifically:
- Hosted: not standard. We can support a temporary 90-day retention for Hosted tenants with an operational ticket + security review. 180 days would trigger a higher-risk exception: we require a written request, CS + Security joint approval, and a contract amendment (DocuSign). We can provide the evidence artifacts listed above once approved.
- Dedicated / Private: configurable at the tenant level; retention can be extended to 180 days subject to the customer's dedicated configuration and standard change control. Documentation and artifacts are straightforward for those modes.

4) Artifacts required from Atlas for the exception review:
- Formal signed request from Atlas security listing exact data classes to retain (plaintext vs. metadata).
- Expected retention timeframe and retention end-of-life process.
- Intended use case and who will have access (roles).

5) Timeline: assuming Atlas signs the formal request and confirms scope, Security + Legal will need 5–7 business days to review and prepare the evidence pack. If engineering changes are needed for Hosted config, add an additional 5–10 business days.

I'll attach our internal checklist (sig-caiq-evidence-checklist.pdf) that outlines deliverables. Markus / Priyom, let me know if you want me to draft the approval memo for Legal.

– Neha Kapoor
Director, Information Security | Redwood Inference

Attachments: sig-caiq-evidence-checklist.pdf


From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@atlasdata.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Sullivan <sullivan@atlasdata.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ: retention mapping & customer-specific exclusions

Hi Neha / Markus — thanks, that level of detail is helpful. We will prepare the formal signed request and confirm that the scope is "metadata + hashed request IDs + latency/error traces" (no plaintext payloads).

Next steps from Atlas:
- We will email the signed scope request by Monday.
- We are fine with the 5–7 business day Security & Legal review window.
- Once approved, we will need Redwood to produce a short amendment (DocuSign) that adds the retention exception to our contract. Can you confirm who will own the amendment?

Oliver / Markus — please confirm whether Redwood can provision a temporary 90-day Hosted variance while the amendment for 180 days is being worked in the background (that would help our time-to-test).

Thanks —
Priya Menon
Security Program Manager, Atlas Data
